description: Surviving mutants a maintainer has looked at and accepted: equivalent ones (no input can tell them apart from the original) and ones that only make a check stricter. mutation_check.py leaves these out of its report. An entry matches by module, cosmic-ray operator and the stripped text of the source line, so it follows the line when code above it moves and stops matching when the line itself changes. An entry whose line text occurs more than once in its module also names the function it is about in function, and then matches only inside that function. tests/test_mutation_check.py fails when an entry does not match exactly one line. Say in reason why the mutant cannot matter.

accepted.reason: How long cosmic-ray waits for one mutant's tests is a tuning value; 119 or 121 seconds changes no outcome a test can observe.

In spells_a_gated_name() the flattened reading differs from the text only where an unquoted extglob group became *, so a string raw_words() rejects as typed (its stand-in character anywhere, or a quoted character the lexer drops) is rejected flattened too, unless that character sits inside the group. Stopping at the first rejection then skips only a command-string prefilter on a string the gate cannot split; no test input reaches that case, and the outer command is still read flattened by refusal().

accepted.line: for reading in (text, *(flattened[:1] if flattened else ())):
accepted.reason: The surviving variant is [:2], which also reads the extglob group's own text as a command string. That only adds a reading to a check whose readings each can only add a refusal, so it is stricter, never weaker; the [:0] variant, which drops the flattened reading, is killed.
How long build() waits before retrying a dropped base pull is a tuning value; 14 or 16 seconds changes no outcome a test can observe, and the tests read the constant rather than restating it.

accepted.line: candidates.extend(word[start:] for start in range(1, len(word)))
accepted.reason: In builtin_assigned_environment() the surviving variants are range(0, ...) and range(2, ...). range(0, ...) also reads the whole option word, dash included, and no REFUSED_ENVIRONMENT pattern starts with a dash, so it can never match. range(2, ...) drops only the tail that starts at the first option letter, and that tail names a variable only when the option letter is part of the name, as in `read -HOME`; read, mapfile and readarray reject such a word as an invalid option and assign nothing. Every tail that starts after a real option letter (`read -aHOME`, `read -raHOME`) is still read.

The surviving variant is split("[", 2)[0]. Splitting further changes only the parts after the first [, and [0] is the text before it either way; the split("[", 0) variant, which keeps the subscript, is killed.
